name: giant spider
desc: To snare its prey, a giant spider spins elaborate webs or shoots sticky strands of webbing from its abdomen. Giant spiders are most commonly found underground, making their lairs on ceilings or in dark, web-filled crevices. Such lairs are often festooned with web cocoons holding past victims.

special_abilities.name: spider climb
special_abilities.desc: The spider can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

special_abilities.name: web sense
special_abilities.desc: While in contact with a web, the spider knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

special_abilities.name: web walker
special_abilities.desc: The spider ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

actions.name: bite
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage, and the target must make a DC 11 Constitution saving throw, taking 9 (2d8) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If the poison damage reduces the target to 0 hit points, the target is stable but poisoned for 1 hour, even after regaining hit points, and is paralyzed while poisoned in this way.

actions.name: web
actions.desc: Ranged Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. Hit: The target is restrained by webbing. As an action, the restrained target can make a DC 12 Strength check, bursting the webbing on a success. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; hp 5; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage).

lore:
The Giant Spider, or *Aranea Titanus*, is a scourge of the sunless places. Found primarily in the choked depths of the Whispering Woods or the lightless veins of the earth, these chitinous horrors are masters of the unseen trap. They do not merely spin webs; they architect labyrinths of adhesive silk capable of halting a charging warhorse.

Their hunting is a study in patience. A spider senses the subtle tremors of a heartbeat through its many-jointed legs, waiting until the prey is hopelessly entwined before delivering a paralyzing strike. In local folklore, they are known as the "Silent Weavers." Old wives' tales suggest that to hear the click of their mandibles is to hear the shears of Fate itself. Some forest clans believe these creatures are the reincarnated souls of traitors, forever weaving shrouds for those they once betrayed. To find a silver strand across your path is a dire omen—a warning that you have entered a domain where the hunter is never seen, only felt. Tread softly, traveler; the web is older than the road.
